footnotes: p. 203 n. 1: For the text see Naville, Todtenbuch, Bd. I., Bll. 137, 138.
notes: Section: from line numeral '2.' (ànet') on p. 203 under 'Appendix.' (footnote 1) to the end of p. 208 (seśet 'the fire,', line 27). Line numerals in range: 2-27; '11.' (p. 205) falls inside mert - f and '27.' (p. 208) inside seśeṭ - nà, so those words are assigned to the preceding line. Pages 204, 206, 208 carry the running head '[Plate XXXII.'; plate field kept as 'App.' per the brief example. No rubric overlines seen in this range. Budge prints a tall thin grey dashed vertical line after many words/suffixes (after ḥr in ḥrāu-θen, after àpu, ānχiu, maāt etc.); it is coded Z1 with an unsure note each time - it may be a divider/marker rather than a sign. Restorations in the hieroglyph line: [A1] in àb - à (p. 205, line 10); '[' ... ']' around àu ... ṭes (p. 208, line 25); an unclosed '[' before seśet (p. 208, line 25) that is not closed by the end of p. 208. Words with no hieroglyph above them: 'en' (by) at the end of p. 205 line 13 (signs empty). Two-part transliterations without hyphen ('ḥer entet', 'sep sen', 'ḥer mā') are split into two words sharing the English gloss. Recurring Budge-type sign shapes coded consistently: the stalk with knot on oval base = M6 approx (tr / Ta-merà); the loop with crossed tails = V22 approx (χer, meḥtet, Fenχu); the 'ρ' hook = F51 approx; the 'ΣΣ' sign = N23 approx; the small slanted cone = M44 approx; the long-armed seated man = A2; the phallus-like horizontal sign = D53 (baḥ, meter, āa); the flat slab with small tie = Y1, the rounded slab with lump = D46 (ànet' last sign Y1 is doubtful, could be D46).
